audit.whatIsWrong: early and whys[0] both say Chomp heals you — 'Chomp heals you and strips his AD', 'Chomp bites through the wave, steals his AD and heals you'.
audit.why: Chomp does not heal. Riot's text: 'Trundle bites his opponent, dealing damage, briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage.' The healing in Trundle's kit is King's Tribute, which pays out when a unit dies near him, and Frozen Domain, which raises healing from all sources while he stands on it. Crediting the bite with the sustain hides the two things a player actually has to position for: standing near dying minions, and standing on the zone.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps Attack Damage on a flat 3.5s and briefly slows. The sustain is King's Tribute off dying minions, amplified by Frozen Domain.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Q Chomp; P King's Tribute; W Frozen Domain)

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Stake is never named anywhere in either layer. report[8] gets as far as 'his damage is AP' and stops.
audit.why: This is the mechanic that makes his execute theme coherent, and it is absent. Silver Stake deals additional magic damage on-hit, increased based on the target's MISSING health — so every auto he lands on a low Trundle hits harder than the last, and Soul Ignition hands him the attack speed to apply it. The entry's rule of 'end fights above his floor' is correct but unexplained; with the passive stated, the player understands that lingering at low HP is not merely execute risk, it is a rising damage multiplier feeding into the execute.
audit.corrected: Silver Stake adds magic damage on every attack, scaled to how much health you are missing — and Soul Ignition's attack speed is how he applies it. Low HP makes each of his autos bigger, then Purgatory finishes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (P Silver Stake, onHit; W Soul Ignition attack speed; R Purgatory execute)

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] states 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Soul Ignition ends with a heal: 'At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' Grievous Wounds reduces healing whatever produces it, so anti-heal is not optional — it is timing-critical. The refund arrives when the burn expires, so the Grievous Wounds application has to land during the effect, not after it, which is a sequencing instruction the entry currently tells the player to skip entirely.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds has to be on him while Soul Ignition is burning — the refund pays out when the duration ends, so applying it afterwards is too late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither ultimate carries a number. mid says 'track his ult before every engage', spikes[1] says 'engage when his R is down', and Ritual Nails is described as a poke with no cooldown ('walk him down whenever his Q Ritual Nails poke misses').
audit.why: Purgatory and Subjugate are both 120/100/80. They come up together at every rank, so this is a mirrored timer and the fight is decided by who spends theirs first — which is exactly the entry's 'bait the totem' advice, now with a reason. Ritual Nails is 10/9/8/7/6 at 950 range, so a whiffed set really is a window early and barely one late. Ashen Pursuit is a flat 10s at every rank with a mana cost that climbs 30 to 70 as he ranks it, so it never gets faster, only more expensive.
audit.corrected: Purgatory 120/100/80 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — mirrored at every rank. Ritual Nails 10s at rank 1 down to 6s. Ashen Pursuit a flat 10s at every rank.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (Q cd 10/9/8/7/6 range 950; E cd 10 cost 30/40/50/60/70; R cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].t reads 'Burn your gap-closer while his E is up', and wants.foe[2] says he uses 'E Ashen Pursuit resets to dodge your Pillar'.
audit.why: Trundle has no gap-closer. His only positioning tool is Pillar of Ice at 21s at rank 1, and the correct instruction is to bank it for the window after Ashen Pursuit is spent rather than to spend it into an exit he still holds. Separately, 'Ashen Pursuit resets' misreads the kit — the reset on it is an ATTACK reset ('dashing to attack his next target'), not a cooldown reset, so there is no repeated blink to dodge with.
audit.corrected: Bank Pillar of Ice's 21 seconds for the window after Ashen Pursuit is spent. The reset on that ability is an attack reset, not a cooldown one — it is a flat 10s either way.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (E Ashen Pursuit, cd 10, dash + autoReset)

audit.why: The chart and the prose agree here, which is rare in this file: Trundle takes Levels 1 through 5, Level 6 is Skill, first item is Locke, two-plus items is Skill. That matches the packet's 50.81% over 248 games and matches the mechanics — Chomp on a flat 3.5s plus King's Tribute beats a champion who pays his own health to trade, and the lane only turns when Purgatory and an AP item arrive together. No stage argues against its own label.

edits.after: Levels 1-4 are your playground. Chomp saps his AD on a flat 3.5s while Soul Ignition burns his own health bar to trade, and King's Tribute heals you off the wave - fight on your ice, hold Pillar for the window after Ashen Pursuit, and tax every CS he steps up to take.

edits.before: At 6 the lane turns into a timing war. Subjugate drains him in any committed fight, but a saved R Purgatory totem can execute you mid-drain, so track his ult before every engage. Once his first AP item finishes, his burst plus execute genuinely kills you - respect the spike and stop taking free-looking fights.

notes: BIGGEST ADD: Silver Stake is never named in either layer, yet it is what makes his whole execute pattern work — his on-hit magic damage scales with the target's MISSING health, and Soul Ignition supplies the attack speed to apply it. The entry's standing rule 'end fights above his floor' was correct but unexplained; now the player knows that staying low is a rising damage multiplier, not just execute risk. CORRECTED: Chomp was credited with healing in two places. It saps Attack Damage and briefly slows — the healing is King's Tribute off dying minions, amplified by Frozen Domain, and that difference changes where the player stands. CORRECTED: report[8] told the player anti-heal is optional. Soul Ignition heals back a portion of the self-damage when its duration ends, so Grievous Wounds is not optional, it is timed — it has to be on him during the burn. CORRECTED: 'Burn your gap-closer while his E is up' — Trundle has no gap-closer. The tool at stake is Pillar of Ice at 21s. Also fixed 'Ashen Pursuit resets': the reset in that ability is an ATTACK reset, not a cooldown reset; it is a flat 10s at every rank, and its mana cost climbs 30 to 70 as he ranks it. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: (1) the kit file's derived flags put trueDamage and grounding on Soul Ignition and Purgatory, but Riot's descriptions mention neither — the true damage most plausibly refers to Soul Ignition's self-damage — so I did not claim either in the text. (2) breakdown.cooldowns says Ashen Pursuit 'resets on takedowns'; nothing in Riot's text for E or for Purgatory says so, and I removed the claim rather than restate it. (3) phases[0].why and breakdown.early call him 'a 125-range' champion; attack range is not in the kit file, so I left both untouched. (4) Purgatory's execute threshold — the entry uses '~15%' in phases[4].why; the kit gives no number, so I kept the sentence's structure and did not import a figure.
